# ------------------------------------------------------------------
## INCLUDING THE PARACONFORMITY ##
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# -------------------------------------
## Set the fixed 50-yr temporal bins ##
# -------------------------------------

# ------- Baiau Superior -------

# Data frame & Pre-treatment

```{r}

# Initial raw unified dataframe:
baiau.sup.df <- read.csv("Select your directory/Unified_raw_dataframes/baiau_superior_raw_unified_data_frame.csv", sep = ";")

#-------------------------------
# Fixed 50yr temporal bins
#-------------------------------

# Create the sample-age table carefully:
ba_sample_ages <- baiau.sup.df %>%
  dplyr::distinct(sample, mean.age, top.age, bottom.age) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    age.interval = bottom.age - top.age
  )

# How many samples above the 50 years?
ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::filter(age.interval > 50) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(age.interval))  

# A summary of the values:
ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(age.interval)),
    min_interval = min(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_interval = quantile(age.interval, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_interval = median(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_interval = mean(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_interval = quantile(age.interval, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_interval = max(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_over_200 = sum(age.interval > 200, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# How many years per interval?
bin_width <- 50

# Diagnose crossing 50-year intervals:
ba_sample_ages_50 <- ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    interval_mean = floor(mean.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_top = floor(top.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_bottom = floor(bottom.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    crosses_50_boundary = interval_top != interval_bottom
  )

ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    median_interval = median(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_interval = mean(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_interval = max(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_crossing = sum(crosses_50_boundary, na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_crossing = mean(crosses_50_boundary, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_over_50 = sum(age.interval > 50, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# Assign samples to 50-year bins by mean age: 
ba_sample_ages_50 <- ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    interval_start = floor(mean.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_end = interval_start + bin_width,
    interval_50 = paste0(interval_start, "-", interval_end, " cal yr BP")
  )

# How many samples per interval?
sample_distribution_50 <- ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::count(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start)

sample_distribution_50

# Join to the long-format data frame:
baiau.sup.df.50 <- baiau.sup.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
      dplyr::select(sample, interval_start, interval_end, interval_50),
    by = "sample"
  )

# Diatom counts: sum valves by interval and taxon
ba.diatom_counts_50 <- baiau.sup.df.50 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50, Species_ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_valves = sum(No, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create the community matrix:
ba.diatom_counts_50 <- ba.diatom_counts_50 %>%     # The main input for sample coverage & diversity estimates!
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Species_ID,
    values_from = total_valves,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start)

ba.comm_50 <- ba.diatom_counts_50 %>%
  dplyr::select(-interval_start, -interval_end, -interval_50)

```

# -----------------------
## Diversity estimates ##
# -----------------------

# ------- Baiau Superior -------

# Sample coverage & diversity estimates

```{r}

# ---------------- Max coverage estimation ---------------------------------

ba.cov <- C_target(ba.comm_50, factor = 2) #It's not recommended a factor>2. 

# ---------------- Diversity indexes --------------------------------------

# Transpose the matrix (required):
ba.comm_50_t <- t(ba.comm_50) 

# Diversity estimates (iNEXT package):
ba.estimates_50 <- estimateD(ba.comm_50_t,
                       q = c(0, 1, 2),
                       datatype = "abundance",
                       base = "coverage",
                       level = 0.96, 
                       nboot = 500, 
                       conf = 0.95)


#To get the qD & upper-lower confidence limits:
ba.estimates.grouped <- subset(ba.estimates_50, select = c(1, 3:4, 6:8))

#To separate the different diversity estimators and name them properly:
ba.estimates.sep <- ba.estimates.grouped %>%
  mutate(
    Hill.spp.rich = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  Hill.spp.rich.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
   Hill.spp.rich.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  exp.shannon = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ unlist(qD),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
   exp.shannon.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  exp.shannon.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ unlist(qD),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::select(-qD, -qD.LCL, -qD.UCL)

#Removing the Order.q variable: 
ba.estimates.sep <- ba.estimates.sep %>% dplyr::select(-Order.q)

#To create the estimator's data frames, separated:
exp.shannon.df <- ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, exp.shannon, exp.shannon.LCL, exp.shannon.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(exp.shannon, exp.shannon.LCL, exp.shannon.UCL)

simpson.df <-  ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, inv.simpson, inv.simpson.LCL, inv.simpson.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(inv.simpson, inv.simpson.LCL, inv.simpson.UCL)

richness.df <-  ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, Hill.spp.rich, Hill.spp.rich.LCL, Hill.spp.rich.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(Hill.spp.rich, Hill.spp.rich.LCL, Hill.spp.rich.UCL)

#All indexes at once:
ba.estimates.merged <- richness.df %>% 
  full_join(exp.shannon.df, by = c("Assemblage", "Method")) %>% 
  full_join(simpson.df, by = c("Assemblage", "Method"))

#Rename the Assemblage column as sample & customise it:
colnames(ba.estimates.merged)[colnames(ba.estimates.merged) == "Assemblage"] <- "sample"

baiau.sup.estimates.df <- ba.estimates.merged %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample = as.numeric(gsub("data", "", sample))
  )

# Evenness (Pielou's J):
baiau.sup.estimates.df <- baiau.sup.estimates.df %>% 
  group_by(sample) %>% 
  mutate(pielou = exp.shannon/Hill.spp.rich) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Create an interval lookup table:
interval_lookup <- baiau.sup.df.50 %>%
  dplyr::distinct(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50) %>%  # Avoid the mismatch between the number of observations (37 vs. 162).
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample = dplyr::row_number(),
    age_mid = (interval_start + interval_end) / 2,
    age_interval = paste0(interval_start, "-", interval_end, " cal yr BP")
  )

baiau.sup.estimates.df <- baiau.sup.estimates.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    interval_lookup,
    by = "sample"
  )

```

# -------------------------------
## Segmented vs. Linear models ##
# -------------------------------

# Homemade functions

```{r}

# Function for segmented model summary extraction:
extract_segmented_summary <- function(lm_model, seg_model, metric_name) {
  
  bp_ci <- confint(seg_model)
  slope_values <- slope(seg_model)$age_mid
  aic_values <- AIC(lm_model, seg_model)
  davies <- segmented::davies.test(lm_model, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric_name,
    selected_model = "segmented",
    breakpoint = seg_model$psi[, "Est."],
    breakpoint_LCL = bp_ci[, "CI(95%).low"],
    breakpoint_UCL = bp_ci[, "CI(95%).up"],
    davies_p = davies$p.value,
    AIC_linear = aic_values$AIC[1],
    AIC_segmented = aic_values$AIC[2],
    delta_AIC = aic_values$AIC[1] - aic_values$AIC[2],
    slope1 = slope_values["slope1", "Est."],
    slope1_LCL = slope_values["slope1", "CI(95%).l"],
    slope1_UCL = slope_values["slope1", "CI(95%).u"],
    slope2 = slope_values["slope2", "Est."],
    slope2_LCL = slope_values["slope2", "CI(95%).l"],
    slope2_UCL = slope_values["slope2", "CI(95%).u"]
  )
}

# Function for linear model summary extraction:
extract_linear_summary <- function(lm_model, metric_name) {
  
  lm_summary <- summary(lm_model)
  coefs <- coef(lm_summary)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric_name,
    selected_model = "linear",
    breakpoint = NA_real_,
    breakpoint_LCL = NA_real_,
    breakpoint_UCL = NA_real_,
    davies_p = NA_real_,
    AIC_linear = AIC(lm_model),
    AIC_segmented = NA_real_,
    delta_AIC = NA_real_,
    slope1 = coefs["age_mid", "Estimate"],
    slope1_LCL = NA_real_,
    slope1_UCL = NA_real_,
    slope2 = NA_real_,
    slope2_LCL = NA_real_,
    slope2_UCL = NA_real_,
    linear_p = coefs["age_mid", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    r_squared = lm_summary$r.squared,
    adj_r_squared = lm_summary$adj.r.squared
  )
}

# Function for segmented predictions:
make_segmented_predictions <- function(data, seg_model, response, n = 300) {
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    age_mid = seq(
      min(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = n
    )
  )
  
  pred_df$fit <- predict(seg_model, newdata = pred_df)
  pred_df$response <- response
  pred_df$breakpoint <- seg_model$psi[, "Est."]
  
  pred_df
}

# Function for linear predictions:
make_linear_predictions <- function(data, lm_model, response, n = 300) {
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    age_mid = seq(
      min(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = n
    )
  )
  
  pred_df$fit <- predict(lm_model, newdata = pred_df)
  pred_df$response <- response
  
  pred_df
}


```

# ------- Baiau Superior -------

# Fit the segmented & linear models & exploring the trends

```{r}

# Data frame with the diversity estimates:
baiau.sup.estimates.df <- read.csv("Select your directory/Diversity_estimates/With_paraconformity/baiau.sup.estimates.df.csv", sep = ";")

# Initial pre-visualisation:
ggplot(baiau.sup.estimates.df, aes(x = age_mid, y = Hill.spp.rich)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1,
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# -------------------- Linear or segmented regression? --------------------

#i) --------- Species richness ---------

# Fit the initial linear model:
ba.richness.lm <- lm(Hill.spp.rich ~ age_mid, data = baiau.sup.estimates.df)

# Fit the segmented model:
ba.richness.seg <- segmented(ba.richness.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

# Model outputs:
summary(ba.richness.seg)
confint(ba.richness.seg)


AIC(ba.richness.lm, ba.richness.seg)

davies.test(ba.richness.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid)

slope(ba.richness.seg)

#ii) --------- Exponential of Shannon diversity (H') ---------

# Fit the initial linear model:
ba.shannon.lm <- lm(exp.shannon ~ age_mid, data = baiau.sup.estimates.df)

# Fit the segmented model:
ba.shannon.seg <- segmented(ba.shannon.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

# Model outputs:
summary(ba.shannon.seg)
confint(ba.shannon.seg)

AIC(ba.shannon.lm, ba.shannon.seg)

davies.test(ba.shannon.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)

slope(ba.shannon.seg)

#iii) --------- Evenness (Pielou's J) ---------

# Fit the initial linear model:
ba.evenness.lm <- lm(pielou ~ age_mid, data = baiau.sup.estimates.df)

# Model output:
summary(ba.evenness.lm)

AIC(ba.evenness.lm)

# To keep the comparison with the rest of model for documentation:
ba.evenness.seg <- segmented(ba.evenness.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

summary(ba.evenness.seg)
confint(ba.evenness.seg)

AIC(ba.evenness.lm, ba.evenness.seg)

davies.test(ba.evenness.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)

slope(ba.evenness.seg)

# -------------------- Baiau Superior model summary table --------------------

baiau.sup.model.summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extract_segmented_summary(
    lm_model = ba.richness.lm,
    seg_model = ba.richness.seg,
    metric_name = "Species richness"
  ),
  extract_segmented_summary(
    lm_model = ba.shannon.lm,
    seg_model = ba.shannon.seg,
    metric_name = "Exponential Shannon diversity"
  ),
  extract_linear_summary(
    lm_model = ba.evenness.lm,
    metric_name = "Evenness"
  )
)

baiau.sup.model.summary

# -------------------- Plots (using ggplot) --------------------

# Create predictions:
ba.richness.pred <- make_segmented_predictions(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  seg_model = ba.richness.seg,
  response = "Hill.spp.rich"
)

ba.shannon.pred <- make_segmented_predictions(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  seg_model = ba.shannon.seg,
  response = "exp.shannon"
)

ba.evenness.pred <- make_linear_predictions(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  lm_model = ba.evenness.lm,
  response = "pielou"
)


plot_bain <- function(data, predictions, model, response, y_label,
                      segmented_fit = TRUE) {

  # Age range based only on Baiau Inferior
  x_limits <- range(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (segmented_fit) {

    # Breakpoint and its confidence interval
    bp <- unname(model$psi[1, "Est."])
    bp_ci <- confint(model)
    bp_limits <- as.numeric(
      bp_ci[1, c("CI(95%).low", "CI(95%).up")]
    )

    # Determine line type from each slope's confidence interval
    slopes <- segmented::slope(model)$age_mid

    significant <- slopes[, "CI(95%).l"] > 0 |
                   slopes[, "CI(95%).u"] < 0

    # Include the breakpoint in both segments so the lines meet
    bp_row <- data.frame(
      age_mid = bp,
      fit = as.numeric(
        predict(model, newdata = data.frame(age_mid = bp))
      )
    )

    pred <- predictions[, c("age_mid", "fit")]

    younger <- rbind(pred[pred$age_mid < bp, ], bp_row)
    older   <- rbind(bp_row, pred[pred$age_mid > bp, ])

    younger$segment <- "younger"
    older$segment   <- "older"

    younger$linetype <- if (significant[1]) "solid" else "dashed"
    older$linetype   <- if (significant[2]) "solid" else "dashed"

    predictions <- rbind(younger, older)

  } else {

    # Significance of the overall linear slope
    slope_ci <- confint(model)["age_mid", ]
    significant <- slope_ci[1] > 0 | slope_ci[2] < 0

    predictions$segment <- "all"
    predictions$linetype <- if (significant) "solid" else "dashed"
  }

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = age_mid, y = .data[[response]])) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_line(
      data = predictions,
      aes(
        x = age_mid,
        y = fit,
        linetype = linetype,
        group = segment
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1.2,
      colour = "darkred"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_identity() +
    scale_x_reverse(
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rev(x_limits)) +
    labs(
      x = "Age (cal yr BP)",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 22)
    )

  if (segmented_fit) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp,
        colour = "blue"
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp_limits,
        linetype = "dotted",
        colour = "blue",
        linewidth = 1,
        alpha = 0.7
      )
  }

  p
}

ba.richness.plot <- plot_bain(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  predictions = ba.richness.pred,
  model = ba.richness.seg,
  response = "Hill.spp.rich",
  y_label = "Species richness"
)

ba.shannon.plot <- plot_bain(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  predictions = ba.shannon.pred,
  model = ba.shannon.seg,
  response = "exp.shannon",
  y_label = "Exponential Shannon diversity"
)

ba.evenness.plot <- plot_bain(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.df,
  predictions = ba.evenness.pred,
  model = ba.evenness.lm,
  response = "pielou",
  y_label = "Evenness",
  segmented_fit = FALSE
)

ba.richness.plot
ba.shannon.plot
ba.evenness.plot

ba_diversity_plots <- (ba.richness.plot | ba.shannon.plot | ba.evenness.plot) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Baiau Superior") &
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold", hjust = 0.05),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.text  = element_text(size = 14))

ba_diversity_plots
```

# -------------------------------
## Generalised Additive Models ##
# -------------------------------

# Homemade function to evaluate k value

```{r, Homemade function}

# ---------------- Function to find a suitable k value ----------------

evaluate_gam_k <- function(data, response, predictor, k_min = 3, k_max = 100) {    # Exclude the "weight_var" parameter from the function.
  
  library(mgcv)
  
  results <- data.frame(
    k = integer(),
    edf = numeric(),
    k_index = numeric(),
    p_value = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  formula_base <- paste(response, "~ s(", predictor, ", bs = 'tp', k = %d)", sep = "")
  
  for (k_val in k_min:k_max) {
    
    cat("Fitting model with k =", k_val, "\n")
    
    model_formula <- as.formula(sprintf(formula_base, k_val))
    
    fit <- tryCatch(
      gam(
        model_formula,
        data = data,
        family = gaussian,
        method = "REML"
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("Model failed for k =", k_val, "\n")
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
    
    if (!is.null(fit)) {
      
      kcheck <- tryCatch(
        mgcv::k.check(fit),
        error = function(e) {
          cat("k.check failed for k =", k_val, "\n")
          return(NULL)
        }
      )
      
      if (!is.null(kcheck)) {
        
        edf_val <- sum(fit$edf)
        k_index <- kcheck[1, "k-index"]
        p_val <- kcheck[1, "p-value"]
        
        results <- rbind(
          results,
          data.frame(
            k = k_val,
            edf = edf_val,
            k_index = k_index,
            p_value = p_val
          )
        )
        
      } else {
        cat("No k.check returned for k =", k_val, "\n")
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# ---------------- Function to extract GAM summary information ----------------

extract_gam_summary <- function(model, metric, k_used) {
  
  # Model summary
  sm <- summary(model)
  
  # Smooth table
  smooth_table <- as.data.frame(sm$s.table)
  
  # k-check table
  k_table <- as.data.frame(mgcv::k.check(model))
  
  data.frame(
    metric = metric,
    k = k_used,
    edf = smooth_table[1, "edf"],
    ref_df = smooth_table[1, "Ref.df"],
    F_value = smooth_table[1, "F"],
    p_value = smooth_table[1, "p-value"],
    adj_r_squared = sm$r.sq,
    deviance_explained = sm$dev.expl,
    REML = sm$sp.criterion,
    scale = sm$scale,
    n = length(model$y),
    k_prime = k_table[1, "k'"],
    k_index = k_table[1, "k-index"],
    k_p_value = k_table[1, "p-value"],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

```

```{r, Fit the models}
              family = gaussian,
              method = "REML", #Smoothness selection (lambda). 
              ) 

summary(ba_richness_gam)
```

```{r}

# Helper function to standardise model predictions:
standardise_prediction_df <- function(df,
                                      lake_name,
                                      metric_name,
                                      model_name,
                                      age_col = "age_mid",
                                      fit_col = "metric_fit",
                                      lower_col = "metric_lower",
                                      upper_col = "metric_upper",
                                      se_col = "metric_se") {
  
  df %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      lake = lake_name,
      metric = metric_name,
      model = model_name,
      age_mid = .data[[age_col]],
      fit = as.numeric(.data[[fit_col]]),
      lower = as.numeric(.data[[lower_col]]),
      upper = as.numeric(.data[[upper_col]]),
      se = as.numeric(.data[[se_col]])
    )
}

# Helper function for dual-axis rescaling:
rescale_to_primary <- function(x, primary_range, secondary_range) {
  (x - secondary_range[1]) / diff(secondary_range) * diff(primary_range) + primary_range[1]
}

inverse_to_secondary <- function(x, primary_range, secondary_range) {
  (x - primary_range[1]) / diff(primary_range) * diff(secondary_range) + secondary_range[1]
}

# Plot function:
plot_gam_segmented_dual_axis <- function(df, metric_name, lake_name,
                                         gam_range,
                                         seg_range,
                                         x_limits = c(7600, 0)) {
  
  plot_df <- df %>%
    filter(metric == metric_name,
           lake == lake_name) %>%
    mutate(
      seg_observed_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_observed,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_fit_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_fit,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_lower_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_lower,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_upper_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_upper,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      )
    )
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = age_mid)) +
    
    # GAM uncertainty
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = gam_lower, ymax = gam_upper),
      alpha = 0.18,
      fill = "grey60"
    ) +
    
    # Segmented uncertainty, rescaled to GAM axis
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = seg_lower_scaled, ymax = seg_upper_scaled),
      alpha = 0.12,
      fill = "grey30"
    ) +
    
    # GAM fitted line
    geom_line(
      aes(y = gam_fit),
      linewidth = 1.1,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    
    # Segmented fitted line, rescaled
    geom_line(
      aes(y = seg_fit_scaled),
      linewidth = 1.1,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "black"
    ) +
    
    # GAM observed values: full points
    geom_point(
      aes(y = gam_observed),
      size = 2.2,
      alpha = 0.85,
      shape = 16
    ) +
    
    # Segmented observed values: empty points, rescaled
    geom_point(
      aes(y = seg_observed_scaled),
      size = 2.3,
      alpha = 0.85,
      shape = 21,
      stroke = 0.8,
      fill = "white"
    ) +
    
    scale_x_reverse(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5)
    ) +
    
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = gam_range,
      name = "GAM estimate",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        trans = ~ inverse_to_secondary(
          .,
          primary_range = gam_range,
          secondary_range = seg_range
        ),
        name = "Segmented estimate"
      )
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = lake_name,
      x = "Age (cal yr BP)"
    ) +
    
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = "black"),
      axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "black")
    )
}
```

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
## EXCLUDING THE PARACONFORMITY ##
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# -------------------------------------
## Set the fixed 50-yr temporal bins ##
# --------------------------------------

# ------- Baiau Superior -------

# Data frame & Pre-treatment

```{r}

# Initial raw unified dataframe:
baiau.sup.df <- read.csv("Select your directory/Unified_raw_dataframes/baiau_superior_raw_unified_data_frame.csv", sep = ";")

# Exclude the samples involved within the paraconformity:
baiau.sup.df_filtered <- baiau.sup.df %>%
  filter(!sample %in% 82:92)   # Samples to be excluded

#-------------------------------
# Fixed 50yr temporal bins
#-------------------------------

# Create the sample-age table carefully:
ba_sample_ages <- baiau.sup.df_filtered %>%
  dplyr::distinct(sample, mean.age, top.age, bottom.age) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    age.interval = bottom.age - top.age
  )

# How many samples above the 50 years?
ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::filter(age.interval > 50) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(age.interval))  

# A summary of the values:
ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(age.interval)),
    min_interval = min(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_interval = quantile(age.interval, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_interval = median(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_interval = mean(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_interval = quantile(age.interval, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_interval = max(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_over_200 = sum(age.interval > 200, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# How many years per interval?
bin_width <- 50

# Diagnose crossing 50-year intervals:
ba_sample_ages_50 <- ba_sample_ages %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    interval_mean = floor(mean.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_top = floor(top.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_bottom = floor(bottom.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    crosses_50_boundary = interval_top != interval_bottom
  )

ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    median_interval = median(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_interval = mean(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_interval = max(age.interval, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_crossing = sum(crosses_50_boundary, na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_crossing = mean(crosses_50_boundary, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_over_50 = sum(age.interval > 50, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# Assign samples to 50-year bins by mean age: 
ba_sample_ages_50 <- ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    interval_start = floor(mean.age / bin_width) * bin_width,
    interval_end = interval_start + bin_width,
    interval_50 = paste0(interval_start, "-", interval_end, " cal yr BP")
  )

# How many samples per interval?
sample_distribution_50 <- ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
  dplyr::count(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start)

sample_distribution_50

# Join to the long-format data frame:
baiau.sup.df.50_no_hiatus <- baiau.sup.df_filtered %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    ba_sample_ages_50 %>%
      dplyr::select(sample, interval_start, interval_end, interval_50),
    by = "sample"
  )

# Diatom counts: sum valves by interval and taxon
ba.diatom_counts_50_no_hiatus <- baiau.sup.df.50_no_hiatus %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50, Species_ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_valves = sum(No, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create the community matrix:
ba.diatom_counts_50_no_hiatus <- ba.diatom_counts_50_no_hiatus %>%     # The main input for sample coverage & diversity estimates!
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Species_ID,
    values_from = total_valves,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start)

ba.comm_50_no_hiatus <- ba.diatom_counts_50_no_hiatus %>%
  dplyr::select(-interval_start, -interval_end, -interval_50)
```

# ------- Baiau Superior -------

# Sample coverage & diversity estimates

```{r}

# ---------------- Max coverage estimation ---------------------------------

ba.cov <- C_target(ba.comm_50_no_hiatus, factor = 2) #It's not recommended a factor>2. 

# ---------------- Diversity indexes --------------------------------------

# Transpose the matrix (required):
ba.comm_50_no_hiatus_t <- t(ba.comm_50_no_hiatus) 

# Diversity estimates (iNEXT package):
ba.estimates_50_no_hiatus <- estimateD(ba.comm_50_no_hiatus_t,
                       q = c(0, 1, 2),
                       datatype = "abundance",
                       base = "coverage",
                       level = 0.96, #Sometimes, it's better to take just the first decimals not to get a too high adjustment 
                       nboot = 500, 
                       conf = 0.95)


#To get the qD & upper-lower confidence limits:
ba.estimates.grouped <- subset(ba.estimates_50_no_hiatus, select = c(1, 3:4, 6:8))

#To separate the different diversity estimators and name them properly:
ba.estimates.sep <- ba.estimates.grouped %>%
  mutate(
    Hill.spp.rich = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  Hill.spp.rich.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
   Hill.spp.rich.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 0 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  exp.shannon = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ unlist(qD),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
   exp.shannon.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  exp.shannon.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 1 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ unlist(qD),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson.LCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ qD.LCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  inv.simpson.UCL = case_when(
    Order.q == 2 ~ qD.UCL,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::select(-qD, -qD.LCL, -qD.UCL)

#Removing the Order.q variable: 
ba.estimates.sep <- ba.estimates.sep %>% dplyr::select(-Order.q)

#To create the estimator's data frames, separated:
exp.shannon.df <- ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, exp.shannon, exp.shannon.LCL, exp.shannon.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(exp.shannon, exp.shannon.LCL, exp.shannon.UCL)

simpson.df <-  ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, inv.simpson, inv.simpson.LCL, inv.simpson.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(inv.simpson, inv.simpson.LCL, inv.simpson.UCL)

richness.df <-  ba.estimates.sep %>%
  dplyr::select(Assemblage, Method, Hill.spp.rich, Hill.spp.rich.LCL, Hill.spp.rich.UCL) %>%
  na.omit(Hill.spp.rich, Hill.spp.rich.LCL, Hill.spp.rich.UCL)

#All indexes at once:
ba.estimates.merged <- richness.df %>% 
  full_join(exp.shannon.df, by = c("Assemblage", "Method")) %>% 
  full_join(simpson.df, by = c("Assemblage", "Method"))

#Rename the Assemblage column as sample & customise it:
colnames(ba.estimates.merged)[colnames(ba.estimates.merged) == "Assemblage"] <- "sample"

baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df <- ba.estimates.merged %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample = as.numeric(gsub("data", "", sample))
  )

# Evenness (Pielou's J):
baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df <- baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df %>% 
  group_by(sample) %>% 
  mutate(pielou = exp.shannon/Hill.spp.rich) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Create an interval lookup table:
interval_lookup <- baiau.sup.df.50_no_hiatus %>%
  dplyr::distinct(interval_start, interval_end, interval_50) %>%  # Avoid the mismatch between the number of observations (37 vs. 162).
  dplyr::arrange(interval_start) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample = dplyr::row_number(),
    age_mid = (interval_start + interval_end) / 2,
    age_interval = paste0(interval_start, "-", interval_end, " cal yr BP")
  )

baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df <- baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    interval_lookup,
    by = "sample"
  )


```

# -------------------------------
## Segmented vs. Linear models ##
# -------------------------------

# Homemade functions

```{r}

# Function for segmented model summary extraction:
extract_segmented_summary <- function(lm_model, seg_model, metric_name) {
  
  bp_ci <- confint(seg_model)
  slope_values <- slope(seg_model)$age_mid
  aic_values <- AIC(lm_model, seg_model)
  davies <- segmented::davies.test(lm_model, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric_name,
    selected_model = "segmented",
    breakpoint = seg_model$psi[, "Est."],
    breakpoint_LCL = bp_ci[, "CI(95%).low"],
    breakpoint_UCL = bp_ci[, "CI(95%).up"],
    davies_p = davies$p.value,
    AIC_linear = aic_values$AIC[1],
    AIC_segmented = aic_values$AIC[2],
    delta_AIC = aic_values$AIC[1] - aic_values$AIC[2],
    slope1 = slope_values["slope1", "Est."],
    slope1_LCL = slope_values["slope1", "CI(95%).l"],
    slope1_UCL = slope_values["slope1", "CI(95%).u"],
    slope2 = slope_values["slope2", "Est."],
    slope2_LCL = slope_values["slope2", "CI(95%).l"],
    slope2_UCL = slope_values["slope2", "CI(95%).u"]
  )
}

# Function for linear model summary extraction:
extract_linear_summary <- function(lm_model, metric_name) {
  
  lm_summary <- summary(lm_model)
  coefs <- coef(lm_summary)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric_name,
    selected_model = "linear",
    breakpoint = NA_real_,
    breakpoint_LCL = NA_real_,
    breakpoint_UCL = NA_real_,
    davies_p = NA_real_,
    AIC_linear = AIC(lm_model),
    AIC_segmented = NA_real_,
    delta_AIC = NA_real_,
    slope1 = coefs["age_mid", "Estimate"],
    slope1_LCL = NA_real_,
    slope1_UCL = NA_real_,
    slope2 = NA_real_,
    slope2_LCL = NA_real_,
    slope2_UCL = NA_real_,
    linear_p = coefs["age_mid", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    r_squared = lm_summary$r.squared,
    adj_r_squared = lm_summary$adj.r.squared
  )
}

# Function for segmented predictions:
make_segmented_predictions <- function(data, seg_model, response, n = 300) {
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    age_mid = seq(
      min(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = n
    )
  )
  
  pred_df$fit <- predict(seg_model, newdata = pred_df)
  pred_df$response <- response
  pred_df$breakpoint <- seg_model$psi[, "Est."]
  
  pred_df
}

# Function for linear predictions:
make_linear_predictions <- function(data, lm_model, response, n = 300) {
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    age_mid = seq(
      min(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = n
    )
  )
  
  pred_df$fit <- predict(lm_model, newdata = pred_df)
  pred_df$response <- response
  
  pred_df
}


```

```{r}
ba.richness.seg <- segmented(ba.richness.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

# Model outputs:
summary(ba.richness.seg)
confint(ba.richness.seg)


AIC(ba.richness.lm, ba.richness.seg)

davies.test(ba.richness.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid)

slope(ba.richness.seg)

#ii) --------- Exponential of Shannon diversity (H') ---------

# Fit the initial linear model:
ba.shannon.lm <- lm(exp.shannon ~ age_mid, data = baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df)

# Fit the segmented model:
ba.shannon.seg <- segmented(ba.shannon.lm, seg.Z = ~age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

# Model outputs:
summary(ba.shannon.seg)
confint(ba.shannon.seg)

AIC(ba.shannon.lm, ba.shannon.seg)

davies.test(ba.shannon.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)

slope(ba.shannon.seg)

#iii) --------- Evenness (Pielou's J) ---------

# Fit the initial linear model:
ba.evenness.lm <- lm(pielou ~ age_mid, data = baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df)

# Model output:
summary(ba.evenness.lm)

AIC(ba.evenness.lm)

# To keep the comparison with the rest of model for documentation:
ba.evenness.seg <- segmented(ba.evenness.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid, psi = list(age_mid = 2000))

summary(ba.evenness.seg)
confint(ba.evenness.seg)

AIC(ba.evenness.lm, ba.evenness.seg)

davies.test(ba.evenness.lm, seg.Z = ~ age_mid)

slope(ba.evenness.seg)

# -------------------- Baiau Superior model summary table --------------------

baiau.sup.model.no_hiatus.summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extract_segmented_summary(
    lm_model = ba.richness.lm,
    seg_model = ba.richness.seg,
    metric_name = "Species richness"
  ),
  extract_segmented_summary(
    lm_model = ba.shannon.lm,
    seg_model = ba.shannon.seg,
    metric_name = "Exponential Shannon diversity"
  ),
  extract_linear_summary(
    lm_model = ba.evenness.lm,
    metric_name = "Evenness"
  )
)

baiau.sup.model.no_hiatus.summary

# -------------------- Plots (using ggplot) --------------------

# Create predictions:

  data = baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df,
  seg_model = ba.richness.seg,
  response = "Hill.spp.rich"
)

ba.shannon.pred <- make_segmented_predictions(
  data = baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df,
  seg_model = ba.shannon.seg,

ba.evenness.pred <- make_linear_predictions(

plot_bain <- function(data, predictions, model, response, y_label,
                      segmented_fit = TRUE) {

  # Age range based only on Baiau Inferior
  x_limits <- range(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (segmented_fit) {

    # Breakpoint and its confidence interval
    bp <- unname(model$psi[1, "Est."])
    bp_ci <- confint(model)
    bp_limits <- as.numeric(
      bp_ci[1, c("CI(95%).low", "CI(95%).up")]
    )

    # Determine line type from each slope's confidence interval
    slopes <- segmented::slope(model)$age_mid

    significant <- slopes[, "CI(95%).l"] > 0 |
                   slopes[, "CI(95%).u"] < 0

    # Include the breakpoint in both segments so the lines meet
    bp_row <- data.frame(
      age_mid = bp,
      fit = as.numeric(
        predict(model, newdata = data.frame(age_mid = bp))
      )
    )

    pred <- predictions[, c("age_mid", "fit")]

    younger <- rbind(pred[pred$age_mid < bp, ], bp_row)
    older   <- rbind(bp_row, pred[pred$age_mid > bp, ])

    younger$segment <- "younger"
    older$segment   <- "older"

    younger$linetype <- if (significant[1]) "solid" else "dashed"
    older$linetype   <- if (significant[2]) "solid" else "dashed"

    predictions <- rbind(younger, older)

  } else {

    # Significance of the overall linear slope
    slope_ci <- confint(model)["age_mid", ]
    significant <- slope_ci[1] > 0 | slope_ci[2] < 0

    predictions$segment <- "all"
    predictions$linetype <- if (significant) "solid" else "dashed"
  }

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = age_mid, y = .data[[response]])) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_line(
      data = predictions,
      aes(
        x = age_mid,
        y = fit,
        linetype = linetype,
        group = segment
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1.2,
      colour = "darkred"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_identity() +
    scale_x_reverse(
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rev(x_limits)) +
    labs(
      x = "Age (cal yr BP)",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 22)
    )

  if (segmented_fit) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp,
        colour = "blue"
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp_limits,
        linetype = "dotted",
        colour = "blue",
        linewidth = 1,
        alpha = 0.7
      )
  }

  p
}
```

```{r}
plot_bain <- function(data, predictions, model, response, y_label,
                      segmented_fit = TRUE) {

  # Age range based only on Baiau Inferior
  x_limits <- range(data$age_mid, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (segmented_fit) {

    # Breakpoint and its confidence interval
    bp <- unname(model$psi[1, "Est."])
    bp_ci <- confint(model)
    bp_limits <- as.numeric(
      bp_ci[1, c("CI(95%).low", "CI(95%).up")]
    )

    # Determine line type from each slope's confidence interval
    slopes <- segmented::slope(model)$age_mid

    significant <- slopes[, "CI(95%).l"] > 0 |
                   slopes[, "CI(95%).u"] < 0

    # Include the breakpoint in both segments so the lines meet
    bp_row <- data.frame(
      age_mid = bp,
      fit = as.numeric(
        predict(model, newdata = data.frame(age_mid = bp))
      )
    )

    pred <- predictions[, c("age_mid", "fit")]

    younger <- rbind(pred[pred$age_mid < bp, ], bp_row)
    older   <- rbind(bp_row, pred[pred$age_mid > bp, ])

    younger$segment <- "younger"
    older$segment   <- "older"

    younger$linetype <- if (significant[1]) "solid" else "dashed"
    older$linetype   <- if (significant[2]) "solid" else "dashed"

    predictions <- rbind(younger, older)

  } else {

    # Significance of the overall linear slope
    slope_ci <- confint(model)["age_mid", ]
    significant <- slope_ci[1] > 0 | slope_ci[2] < 0

    predictions$segment <- "all"
    predictions$linetype <- if (significant) "solid" else "dashed"
  }

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = age_mid, y = .data[[response]])) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_line(
      data = predictions,
      aes(
        x = age_mid,
        y = fit,
        linetype = linetype,
        group = segment
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1.2,
      colour = "darkred"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_identity() +
    scale_x_reverse(
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rev(x_limits)) +
    labs(
      x = "Age (cal yr BP)",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 22)
    )

  if (segmented_fit) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp,
        colour = "blue"
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = bp_limits,
        linetype = "dotted",
        colour = "blue",
        linewidth = 1,
        alpha = 0.7
      )
  }

  p
}
```

# Homemade function to evaluate k value

```{r, Homemade function}

# ---------------- Function to find a suitable k value ----------------

evaluate_gam_k <- function(data, response, predictor, k_min = 3, k_max = 100) {    # Exclude the "weight_var" parameter from the function.
  
  library(mgcv)
  
  results <- data.frame(
    k = integer(),
    edf = numeric(),
    k_index = numeric(),
    p_value = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  formula_base <- paste(response, "~ s(", predictor, ", bs = 'tp', k = %d)", sep = "")
  
  for (k_val in k_min:k_max) {
    
    cat("Fitting model with k =", k_val, "\n")
    
    model_formula <- as.formula(sprintf(formula_base, k_val))
    
    fit <- tryCatch(
      gam(
        model_formula,
        data = data,
        family = gaussian,
        method = "REML"
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("Model failed for k =", k_val, "\n")
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
    
    if (!is.null(fit)) {
      
      kcheck <- tryCatch(
        mgcv::k.check(fit),
        error = function(e) {
          cat("k.check failed for k =", k_val, "\n")
          return(NULL)
        }
      )
      
      if (!is.null(kcheck)) {
        
        edf_val <- sum(fit$edf)
        k_index <- kcheck[1, "k-index"]
        p_val <- kcheck[1, "p-value"]
        
        results <- rbind(
          results,
          data.frame(
            k = k_val,
            edf = edf_val,
            k_index = k_index,
            p_value = p_val
          )
        )
        
      } else {
        cat("No k.check returned for k =", k_val, "\n")
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# ---------------- Function to extract GAM summary information ----------------

extract_gam_summary <- function(model, metric, k_used) {
  
  # Model summary
  sm <- summary(model)
  
  # Smooth table
  smooth_table <- as.data.frame(sm$s.table)
  
  # k-check table
  k_table <- as.data.frame(mgcv::k.check(model))
  
  data.frame(
    metric = metric,
    k = k_used,
    edf = smooth_table[1, "edf"],
    ref_df = smooth_table[1, "Ref.df"],
    F_value = smooth_table[1, "F"],
    p_value = smooth_table[1, "p-value"],
    adj_r_squared = sm$r.sq,
    deviance_explained = sm$dev.expl,
    REML = sm$sp.criterion,
    scale = sm$scale,
    n = length(model$y),
    k_prime = k_table[1, "k'"],
    k_index = k_table[1, "k-index"],
    k_p_value = k_table[1, "p-value"],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

```

```{r}

# Helper function to standardise model predictions:
standardise_prediction_df <- function(df,
                                      lake_name,
                                      metric_name,
                                      model_name,
                                      age_col = "age_mid",
                                      fit_col = "metric_fit",
                                      lower_col = "metric_lower",
                                      upper_col = "metric_upper",
                                      se_col = "metric_se") {
  
  df %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      lake = lake_name,
      metric = metric_name,
      model = model_name,
      age_mid = .data[[age_col]],
      fit = as.numeric(.data[[fit_col]]),
      lower = as.numeric(.data[[lower_col]]),
      upper = as.numeric(.data[[upper_col]]),
      se = as.numeric(.data[[se_col]])
    )
}

# Helper function for dual-axis rescaling:
rescale_to_primary <- function(x, primary_range, secondary_range) {
  (x - secondary_range[1]) / diff(secondary_range) * diff(primary_range) + primary_range[1]
}

inverse_to_secondary <- function(x, primary_range, secondary_range) {
  (x - primary_range[1]) / diff(primary_range) * diff(secondary_range) + secondary_range[1]
}

# Plot function:
plot_gam_segmented_dual_axis <- function(df, metric_name, lake_name,
                                         gam_range,
                                         seg_range,
                                         x_limits = c(7600, 0)) {
  
  plot_df <- df %>%
    filter(metric == metric_name,
           lake == lake_name) %>%
    mutate(
      seg_observed_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_observed,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_fit_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_fit,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_lower_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_lower,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      ),
      seg_upper_scaled = rescale_to_primary(
        seg_upper,
        primary_range = gam_range,
        secondary_range = seg_range
      )
    )
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = age_mid)) +
    
    # GAM uncertainty
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = gam_lower, ymax = gam_upper),
      alpha = 0.18,
      fill = "grey60"
    ) +
    
    # Segmented uncertainty, rescaled to GAM axis
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = seg_lower_scaled, ymax = seg_upper_scaled),
      alpha = 0.12,
      fill = "grey30"
    ) +
    
    # GAM fitted line
    geom_line(
      aes(y = gam_fit),
      linewidth = 1.1,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    
    # Segmented fitted line, rescaled
    geom_line(
      aes(y = seg_fit_scaled),
      linewidth = 1.1,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "black"
    ) +
    
    # GAM observed values: full points
    geom_point(
      aes(y = gam_observed),
      size = 2.2,
      alpha = 0.85,
      shape = 16
    ) +
    
    # Segmented observed values: empty points, rescaled
    geom_point(
      aes(y = seg_observed_scaled),
      size = 2.3,
      alpha = 0.85,
      shape = 21,
      stroke = 0.8,
      fill = "white"
    ) +
    
    scale_x_reverse(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5)
    ) +
    
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = gam_range,
      name = "GAM estimate",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        trans = ~ inverse_to_secondary(
          .,
          primary_range = gam_range,
          secondary_range = seg_range
        ),
        name = "Segmented estimate"
      )
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = lake_name,
      x = "Age (cal yr BP)"
    ) +
    
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = "black"),
      axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "black")
    )
}
```

```{r, Baiau Superior}
# -------------------- Create a common age grid for Baiau Superior ------------------------

# Required data frames:
baiau.sup.df <- read.csv("Select your directory/Unified_raw_dataframes/baiau_superior_raw_unified_data_frame.csv", sep = ";")
baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df <- read.csv("Select your directory/Without_paraconformity/baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df.csv", sep = ";")

age_grid <- tibble(
  age_mid = seq(
    from = min(
      c(
        baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df$age_mid,
        baiau.sup.df$mean.age
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    to = max(
      c(
        baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df$age_mid,
        baiau.sup.df$mean.age
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    length.out = 400
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    mean.age = age_mid
  )

# -------------------- Extract CI from the models ------------------------

#Species richness:
ba_richness_gam_pred <- predict(       #  Generalised Additive Model
  ba_richness_gam,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_richness_gam_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_richness_gam_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_richness_gam_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )

ba_richness_seg_pred <- predict(    # Segmented model
  ba.richness.seg,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_richness_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_richness_seg_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_richness_seg_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )

# Exp. Shannon diversity:
ba_shannon_gam_pred <- predict(       #  Generalised Additive Model
  ba_shannon_gam,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_shannon_gam_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_shannon_gam_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_shannon_gam_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )
 
ba_shannon_seg_pred <- predict(        # Segmented model
  ba.shannon.seg,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_shannon_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_shannon_seg_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_shannon_seg_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )

# Evenness (Pielou's J):
ba_evenness_gam_pred <- predict(       #  Generalised Additive Model
  ba_evenness_gam,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_evenness_gam_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_evenness_gam_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_evenness_gam_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )

ba_evenness_seg_pred <- predict(                # (Non-)Segmented model; Actually, predictions come from a linear model!
  ba.evenness.lm,
  newdata = age_grid,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

ba_evenness_fit <- age_grid %>%
  mutate(
    metric_fit = as.numeric(ba_evenness_seg_pred$fit),
    metric_se = as.numeric(ba_evenness_seg_pred$se.fit),
    metric_lower = metric_fit - 1.96 * metric_se,
    metric_upper = metric_fit + 1.96 * metric_se
  )

# -------------------- Standardise predictions -----------------------

# Species richness:
ba_richness_seg_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Segmented model
  df = ba_richness_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Species richness",
  model_name = "Segmented"
)

ba_richness_gam_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Generalised Additive Model
  df = ba_richness_gam_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Species richness",
  model_name = "GAM"
)

# Exp. Shannon diversity:
ba_shannon_seg_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Segmented model
  df = ba_shannon_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Exp.shannon",
  model_name = "Segmented"
)

ba_shannon_gam_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Generalised Additive Model
  df = ba_shannon_gam_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Exp.shannon",
  model_name = "GAM"
)

# Evenness (Pielou's J):
ba_evenness_seg_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Segmented model
  df = ba_evenness_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Evenness",
  model_name = "Segmented"
)

ba_evenness_gam_std <- standardise_prediction_df(    # Generalised Additive Model
  df = ba_evenness_gam_fit,
  lake_name = "Baiau Superior",
  metric_name = "Evenness",
  model_name = "GAM"
)


# Join the three metrics:
ba_estimates_models <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ba_richness_gam_std,
  ba_richness_seg_std,
  ba_shannon_gam_std,
  ba_shannon_seg_std,
  ba_evenness_gam_std,
  ba_evenness_seg_std
)

# -------------------- Data frame with observed values -----------------------

# Species richness:
ba_richness_obs <- baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    lake = "Baiau Superior",
    metric = "Species richness",
    age_mid = age_mid,
    observed = Hill.spp.rich
  )

# Exp. Shannon diversity:
ba_shannon_obs <- baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    lake = "Baiau Superior",
    metric = "Exp.shannon",
    age_mid = age_mid,
    observed = exp.shannon
  )

# Evenness (Pielou's J):
ba_evenness_obs <- baiau.sup.estimates.no_hiatus.df %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    lake = "Baiau Superior",
    metric = "Evenness",
    age_mid = age_mid,
    observed = pielou
  )

# Join the observed values per metric:
ba_estimates_obs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ba_richness_obs,
  ba_shannon_obs,
  ba_evenness_obs
)
```

```{r}
baiau_estimates_models_all <- baiau_estimates_models_all %>%

  baiau_estimates_obs %>%
    transmute(metric, value = observed),

  baiau_estimates_models_all %>%
    transmute(metric, value = lower),

  baiau_estimates_models_all %>%
    transmute(metric, value = upper)
) %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(
    minimum = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
